result.effect: RMSEA .076, CFI .878, TLI .866 after removal versus RMSEA .097, CFI .764, TLI .748 originally

cells.quote: After the removal of items, the fitness scores of the model improved and were closer to the desired cut-off values. The RMSEA is closer to the cut-off value of 0.08, and CFI and TLI are closer to the cut-off value of .95, respectively.
cells.note: This is a comparison of alternative CFA specifications, not an instructional treatment.

D.comparison: one-factor model based on all six subscales, including PF

result.effect: without PF: RMSEA .123, CFI .964, TLI .928; all six subscales: RMSEA .269, CFI .867, TLI .748

cells.quote: Modification indices hinted toward a conflicting relationship between the PF dimension and the other dimensions of the model. Removing the PF dimension from the model resulted in the model shown in Table 5. Although the relative fit indices improve, the new model does not meet the criteria of a good fit concerning the CFI and the TLI.
cells.note: The study interprets PF as potentially ambiguous because interest in professional development may reflect either high competence or perceived knowledge gaps.

cells.quote: Removing the AT dimension from the model resulted in the model shown in Table 6. The final model meets the criteria of a good fit concerning the CFI and the TLI, as well as the RMSEA (see Fig. 2).
cells.note: The study concludes that Professionalization and Attitude do not fit the final overall perceived AI competence model in their current form; the contrast is between alternative CFA specifications.
